comparator.name: Bachelor Informatiekunde (Information Science)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 official guide has 55 EC of compulsory propedeutic courses and 65 EC of fixed postpropedeutic work including 10 EC of research methods and a 5-EC pre-thesis course. It also requires 15 EC selected from six restricted Analytics/Innovation courses, 30 EC of genuine free elective space, and a 15-EC final project: 180 EC. The chosen restricted courses are Python programming, Big Data for Dynamic Systems and Innovation Management. They represent computing, analytics and organisational innovation without treating either Analytics or Innovation as a formal route. The standard 10-EC methods course is selected, rather than its intensive summer version.

alternatives.label: Information systems, organisations and digital society
alternatives.concept: Combines programming, databases, data analysis and system design with organisational change, user needs, research methods, security and responsible technology. It follows OU Informatiekunde’s bridge between computing and management while acknowledging that UCR lacks its formal enterprise-modelling, ontology, project-management and compulsory information-science research sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has sustained computing and data study alongside business, social research and responsible digital systems.
progression: Programming, databases, mathematical and research foundations precede advanced algorithms, machine learning, organisational analysis and governance. All formal prerequisites and term offerings have been checked in the current enriched workbook.

alternatives.label: Data science and computational information
alternatives.concept: Retains programming, databases, organisational context and responsible technology but gives more weight to probability, linear algebra, numerical and systems modelling, algorithms and machine learning. This develops the OU programme’s Analytics restricted-choice direction and data-and-information-management learning line.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum adds mathematical and computational data methods while preserving essential information-systems and organisational study.
progression: Programming, database, research and mathematical foundations precede advanced algorithms, statistics, optimisation and machine learning. All formal prerequisites and term offerings have been checked in the current enriched workbook.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad route, this curriculum replaces four courses focused on product design, organisational leadership, communication and digital transformation with linear algebra, numerical methods, linear systems and advanced statistics. These are genuine consequences of the official Analytics direction and meet the pairwise 30-EC floor.

alternatives.label: Software, computer systems and algorithms
alternatives.concept: Develops OU Informatiekunde’s Programming and Technology learning line through programming, databases, networks and operating systems, software development, algorithms, discrete mathematics and selected AI methods. It is a technical direction within information science, not a claim to reproduce the OU programme’s organisational and management core.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule concentrates on software, computer systems and algorithms, supported by data and mathematics; the label does not imply a complete OU Informatiekunde curriculum.
progression: Programming and mathematical foundations precede advanced software, systems, algorithms and AI. All formal prerequisites and term offerings have been checked in the current enriched workbook.
alternatives.distinctness: This route gives sustained space to networks and operating systems, software development, advanced algorithms and computer-vision/AI work instead of the broad route’s organisation and social-systems courses or the data route’s mathematical modelling emphasis. It differs from each by substantially more than four courses.

candidates.label: Data and information management with analytics

selection.assessment: The closest match covers the overall OU bridge between information systems, organisations, data, programming, security and research. Its formal data-and-information-management learning line and Analytics choice support a more quantitative second route. The separate Programming and Technology line supports a technical software-and-systems third route. The remaining generator-eligible interests are substantively represented in the closest match; all three feasible curricula have distinct organising priorities and pass pairwise 30-EC differences.

notes.text: OU Informatiekunde has dedicated enterprise modelling, ontology engineering, socio-technical security, management accounting, project management, a compulsory 10-EC information-science methods course and a 15-EC final project. UCR offers related systems, data and organisational courses, but its three pathways do not reproduce that full specialist sequence. OU also has 15 EC of restricted Analytics/Innovation choice and 30 EC of genuine open elective space.
